globalRequirements: Audit the implemented Pharos SQL foundation against the frozen technical intent represented by the repository architecture contracts for schema foundation, Claim/Evidence/Provenance, and Incident Core/Projection at this exact source SHA.

Canonical factual layers must remain separate: assertion is not truth; source quality is not evidence independence; Claim truth confidence is not Incident identity confidence; there is no Incident-wide truth-confidence scalar.

Historical/revision data is append-only and exact input revisions/versions are pinned. Corrections, recomputation, duplicate handling, and split handling must append new history rather than rewrite prior factual/provenance history.
System-knowledge time, source time, and asserted world time must remain distinct. Unqualified world facts must not leak onto roots that are intentionally identity/admin-only.

Do not report missing Event grouping, Situation lifecycle, ingestion, learned models, public read API, provider credentials, or product database provisioning as defects; those are explicitly outside this implemented scope.
The audit is read-only. Model findings have no mutation, merge, deploy, or production PASS/FAIL authority.

bundles.name: root/revision/current-pointer/time-axis/lineage foundation
requirements: Root rows may own stable identity, admin state/timestamps, and current pointers only; factual values that belong in versioned structures must not be promoted onto roots.
Revision/version rows are immutable append-only history and current pointers must not cross root ownership boundaries.
Supersedes/parent relationships must preserve root ownership invariants where physically enforceable.
Derived structures must pin exact input revision/version IDs, with policy versions and generic lineage represented explicitly.
PostgreSQL 18 raw SQL is the canonical schema contract; JSON snapshots must not replace exact provenance or revision foreign keys.

bundles.name: Claim, Evidence Unit, Evidence Family, source assessment and frozen assessment policy
requirements: Claim stores what a claimant asserted and Claim Assessment stores system/reviewer inference; these must never collapse into one truth field.
Evidence Unit must preserve source/raw-item/time/rights provenance. Rights-state changes may only become more restrictive and must not synthesize deleted/unavailable content.
Evidence Family represents shared evidentiary origin/independence and must not own or infer source quality.

Scoring-relevant evidence links and assessment contribution snapshots must pin exact Evidence Family revision, Evidence Link, and Source Assessment revision; one Evidence Family contributes at most once per assessment.
Frozen weight/mass/confidence formulas and state thresholds must be applied exactly; do not invent a direct-primary boost or other hidden confidence mutation.

bundles.name: Claim correction/retraction/supersession snapshot and historical non-retroactivity
requirements: A materially different proposition is a new Claim linked through CORRECTS, RETRACTS, SUPERSEDES, or DUPLICATE_ASSERTION_OF rather than an in-place rewrite of proposition identity.
Correction/retraction refs in an Assessment are immutable snapshots of the exact relation identity and correcting Claim version used at that revision.
An attributable correction ref must target the assessed Claim, belong to the correcting Claim, and preserve the required claimant/source attribution relationship.
Later correction relations must not retroactively change earlier Assessment revisions; a new Assessment revision is required.

bundles.name: Incident identity, revisions, Claim membership, property candidates and projection
requirements: Incident root is occurrence identity/admin/current pointers only. Actor, occurrence time, location, action, target/object, cause, quantity, type, and overall truth confidence are forbidden as unqualified root facts.
Incident revisions are append-only and linear; Claim membership pins exact Claim version and remains an occurrence-linkage judgment rather than Claim truth.
Occurrence envelopes are bounded resolution/search aids and concrete envelope sections must trace to basis candidate IDs rather than raw unqualified facts.
Property candidate normalized value/identity/confidence/role/normalizer version is immutable; only the bounded forward administrative normalization-state transitions are allowed.
RESOLVED/PROVISIONAL projection display values must exactly equal selected immutable candidate normalized values; the projection layer must not synthesize an untracked value.

bundles.name: projection trace guards, stale detection, candidate/Claim locking, duplicate and split lineage
requirements: Projection append must revalidate selected/alternative candidates and current Claim roots under deterministic locking before snapshotting exact Claim version/Assessment refs and advancing the current projection pointer.
A candidate derived from an older Claim version cannot be presented as current after the Claim advances; projection staleness must expose that fact and recomputation must append rather than rewrite.
Current projections may use only ACTIVE candidates; retirement/supersession remains historical provenance and cannot be silently reversed.
Duplicate supersession and split operations are non-destructive and must preserve prior memberships, envelopes, candidates, projections, and immutable lineage.
Source-quality diagnostics and independent-evidence-family diagnostics must remain separate.

bundles.name: exact-SHA PostgreSQL validation recipe and cross-layer ordering
requirements: The recipe must validate the exact checked-out source using PostgreSQL 18.6, apply migrations in canonical order, run all relevant contract tests, and leave the checkout clean.
Validation must not require or mutate a product database, Dashboard control database, provider credential, or unrelated repository state.
A validation recipe is verification only and must not silently repair/mutate the source under test.
